title: Elastic Handoff Protocol and Client Guidance
body:
Purpose:
This note defines an "elastic handoff" protocol for the Hosted API streaming surface and SDK guidance for client implementers. The goal is to let clients (mobile, web, server)   
- start an interaction on a low-latency, low-cost path and seamlessly escalate to a higher-fidelity, tool-enabled path when needed, and
- recover/resume partial session state across transient network issues or client restarts without manual reconciliation.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Many apps need partial real-time output with occasional tool calls (search, DB, browser). Current streaming approaches either force a single high-cost path (always tool-enabled) or ad-hoc client hacks to re-issue requests and reconcile outputs.
- We need a clean, observable, and low-friction model for: 1) incremental results, 2) progressive tool invocation, 3) graceful escalation and fallback, and 4) resumable sessions.

Key goals:
- Minimize wasted tokens by preferring a compact, inference-only fast-path until a tool call or explicit escalation is required.
- Provide deterministic handoff semantics so clients can merge partial outputs from multiple paths without duplication.
- Offer a simple SDK surface that hides the underlying multipath and resume mechanics while exposing hooks for debugging/observability.
- Support structured output (JSON schemas) across both fast and heavy paths with a consistent versioning story.

Non-goals:
- Full universal protocol for cross-vendor tool invocation. We provide a Redwood-hosted contract for tool calls and a minimal adapter spec for third-party tool proxies.
- Replacing long-running server-side workflows (these are out of scope).

User stories:
- Mobile chat app: user sees partial streaming suggestions quickly. If a suggestion requires a web lookup, the client triggers an escalation to tool-enabled path; final result merges without duplicate sentences and preserves token accounting.
- Server-side assistant: service keeps a short-lived prefix cached; on surge or user follow-up, it resumes the high-fidelity path and continues the conversation from the cached prefix.
- Multi-device resume: user starts drafting on phone, continues on laptop; the laptop resumes the session at the last acknowledged checkpoint.

High-level protocol concepts:
- Session ID and Segment tokens: every session has a stable session_id. Streaming output is grouped into ordered segments with monotonic segment_index. Segments include an "ack_token" that clients can persist.
- Fast-path vs heavy-path lanes: each request declares a desired lane: "fast" (no tool access, minimal KV/ctx), "heavy" (tool access, longer timeout), or "elastic" (server may promote).
- Handoff event: an explicit event emitted by server that indicates lane promotion/demotion and provides mapping info to merge subsequent segments deterministically.
- Resume token: short opaque string generated by server representing last committed prefix/snapshot. Clients pass resume_token to continue without replaying entire history.

Message primitives (informal):
- Request headers/fields: {session_id, segment_index_start, lane_preference, resume_token?, schema_version?} 
- Server stream frames: 
  - FRAME_START(segment_index, ack_token, lane) -- start of a segment
  - FRAME_CHUNK(text | chunk_type) -- streaming bytes or structured fragments
  - FRAME_TOOL_CALL(tool_id, call_id, spec) -- indicates a tool invocation (only on heavy lane)
  - FRAME_HANOFF_PROMOTE(prev_ack_token, new_ack_token, mapping_info) -- promotion notice and deterministic reconciliation hints
  - FRAME_COMMIT(ack_token) -- segment committed, safe to persist
  - FRAME_END(segment_index) -- segment finished

Deterministic merging rules (client-side):
- Merge by segment_index order. If FRAME_HANDOFF_PROMOTE is observed, subsequent segments include mapping_info that tells client which tokens are authoritative (e.g., "use heavy lane tokens for sentences ending after offset X").
- If overlapping text appears between fast-path and heavy-path outputs, prefer the heavy-path authoritative region as indicated by mapping_info. Where mapping_info is missing, prefer latest segment but log a non-fatal merge conflict.

SDK ergonomics (principles):
- Keep main SDK surface simple: startStreaming(sessionId, {lane: 'elastic'|'fast'|'heavy', schema: 'assistant_v2'}) -> returns StreamHandle
- StreamHandle provides: on('partial'), on('tool_request'), on('handoff'), checkpoint() -> returns resume_token, resume(resume_token)
- Default behavior: SDK persists latest FRAME_COMMIT ack_token to local storage (mobile: secure local DB) and handles automatic resume on reconnect if resume_token present.
- Advanced hooks: allow apps to opt out of automatic promotion so they can show UI prompts before enabling tools (privacy control).

Sample client sequence (mobile optimistic flow):
1) startStreaming(sessionA, {lane: 'elastic'})
2) receive partial FRAME_CHUNKs on fast lane, UI shows typed tokens
3) server emits FRAME_HANDOFF_PROMOTE (because model requested a web search)
4) SDK raises on('handoff') with a small preview and returns control to app; app shows "fetching web results" indicator
5) app may call allowToolInvocation(true) or leave false to cancel promotion
6) if allowed, server continues on heavy lane, emits FRAME_TOOL_CALL (search), then returns FRAME_COMMIT
7) SDK receives FRAME_COMMIT -> checkpoint() stores resume_token locally

Structured output and schema compatibility:
- Schema version is a required request field when client expects typed response. Server will attach schema_version in FRAME_START and validate tool responses to that schema before emitting FRAME_COMMIT.
- Backward compatibility: server will include schema_migration_hint in FRAME_HANDOFF_PROMOTE if heavy lane upgrades to a newer schema. SDK exposes this hint via on('schema-change') so apps can degrade gracefully.

Telemetry and observability:
- Events to collect: promotion_requested, promotion_accepted, promotion_cancelled, resume_attempt, resume_success, merge_conflict (non-fatal), tool_call_latency, token_savings_estimate (delta between fast+heavy), lane_switch_latency.
- SDK should tag telemetry with route/model, session_id (hashed), and client platform.
- Console: add a per-session timeline view that shows segments, lane changes, tool calls, and merge conflicts. Useful for support and debugging.

Security and privacy considerations:
- Promotions that enable tool invocation should require explicit client consent for mobile/web (configurable per-key).
- Resume tokens must be short-lived and bound to the client_id unless customer config allows cross-device resume.
- Tool-call payloads should scrub PII unless customer has allowed extended telemetry for debugging.

Developer migration story (for existing hosted streaming users):
- Backwards compatible: existing streaming endpoints default to lane='fast' equivalently. No change unless client opts into elastic/heavy lanes.
- Migration steps: opt-in flag in API key; SDK vX will default to not persist resume tokens unless an app explicitly enables cross-device resume.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (SDK/console only): limited to internal beta customers, opt-in key flag, server-side feature gate (1 month).
- Beta: expand to early partners, enable telemetry dashboards, add migration docs (2 months).
- GA: enable by default for new hosted plans, docs, and sample apps (4–6 months).

Open questions / decisions to make:
- How long should resume_token TTL be by default? Proposal: 24 hours for mobile sessions, configurable up to 30 days for enterprise (requires explicit consent).
- Mapping_info format: simple authoritative range vs token-level diffs. Proposal: start with authoritative range markers to keep client merging simple.
- Billing clarity: how to bill tokens generated on fast-path vs heavy-path when handoff occurs mid-segment? Proposal: attribute tokens to lane that produced final committed output (heavy lane wins) and surface pre-commit token counts in debug telemetry.

Implementation notes / engineering TODOs:
- [ENG] extend streaming frame wire format in the gateway (proto changes + backwards compat) - Rohit
- [SDK] persistence layer and resume API for mobile JS + Kotlin + Swift - Maya
- [PRODUCT] opt-in key config, console toggle, telemetry dashboard - Jonah
- Create integration tests for merge conflicts, cross-device resume, and schema migrations.

Nearby artifacts and references:
- quick-play app: samples/elastic-handoff/demo (internal repo)
- design mockups: slack:#product-hosted pinned handoff-mockup-2025-01-02
- related tickets: JIRA-API-3210 (stream frame schema v2), JIRA-API-3199 (resume_token security)

Next steps (short term):
- Sync with runtime team to validate frame semantics and cost implications
- Prototype SDK checkpoint/resume behavior in mobile sample app
- Draft console UX for per-session timeline and handoff permission toggle

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a draft focused on pragmatic developer ergonomics. Expect multiple iterations on mapping_info and billing behavior. Please flag any compatibility concerns with the gateway or model runtime that would make deterministic merging brittle.
